title: Duke Site
summary: The Duke Site is associated with shell-midden archaeology near the Hands Creek and Ashawagh landscape. Public mapping gives only broad area context and does not identify shell midden locations, parcels, or routes.
map_geometry_source: Broad public orientation point on Hands Creek Road from OSM/Nominatim and Directus text; not the exact shell midden, parcel, or route.
why_this_matters: The discovery of an shell midden at the Duke Site near Hand's Creek provides tangible physical evidence of the deep Indigenous occupation surrounding the Ashawagh settlement. Unearthing these everyday material remains helps map the extensive ways Native communities historically utilized Long Island's coastal resources and preserves the physical footprint of their daily lives.
preservation_content: Duke Site involves sensitive shell-midden archaeology in the broad Hands Creek Road area. Exact midden locations, parcels, and access routes are withheld.
